name: reg-exp-value-test-30e03bfeee/regexp-value-negative-e.bal
spec_references: ## Expressions: "Currently support `nil-literal`, `boolean-literal`, `numeric-literal` and `string-literal` only"; the supported expression list includes XML and string templates, but not regular-expression templates.

## Import declarations (under # Subset restrictions): "Only following lang libraries with given methods/types are supported"; `ballerina/lang.string` lists `Char` and string operations, but not `RegExp`.
reason: The case asserts compile-time rejection of invalid regular-expression templates, including reversed ranges, invalid quantifiers, duplicate/conflicting flags, escapes, Unicode properties, and empty character classes. Regular-expression template syntax and its validation are outside the supported expression list; the explicitly used string:RegExp type is also absent from the allowed lang.string types. These essential unsupported features make the whole case a feature request.
unsupported_constructs: Regular-expression template expressions (re backtick syntax) and their compile-time syntax/semantic validation
test_design_notes: Negative tests remain in scope when exercising supported grammar or types, but these assertions specifically require unsupported regular-expression syntax and validation.
The final malformed template and trailing error marker also exercise parser recovery; this does not remove the essential regular-expression dependency.
